selection_rationale: HIMS topped the shortlist (score 74.6): down 24.1% on the week on 3x volume after a Q3 report with the first subscriber decline, a third EBITDA guidance cut and a Q4 revenue guide flat with Q3, plus five states joining the FTC suit, and it crossed below its 200-week line. It is the most recognisable name on the list with a live opportunity-or-trap debate and deep disclosure. The piece answers what the 49% revenue growth is made of and what the Eucalyptus deferred payments do to the share count. AAON and MOD rose on earnings and a takeover report; IONS fell on trial setbacks.

selection_rationale: A market-wide AI sell-off put eight of the ten shortlisted names down 25-34%, mostly on sector beta (quantum, neoclouds, space). NVDA's 23% fall had company-specific causes: the CEO's resignation, a delayed 10-Q and a reported SEC accounting probe, in the world's most widely held stock, now sitting on its 200-week line. The piece answers whether the earnings are real and whether 7.6x forward earnings is cheap or a peak-cycle multiple. Passed on SMMT (single-asset trial readout), GLBE (smaller beat-and-raise sell-off) and the sector-beta names.

selection_rationale: AMBA fell 40.2% after guiding Q4 revenue to $70-75M against about $112M expected, blaming the memory price spike, and now sits 46% below its 200-week line. It has a company-specific cause, years of filings and a live debate: temporary shock and takeover candidate, or a business whose economics never covered its stock comp. KYMR scored slightly higher on a Phase 2b win but has no product revenue to support the format; INSM is a merger-arb pin on Sanofi's bid; NTNX and ANF were smaller stories.
